children: Uranium futures in the US were at $90 per pound, remaining close to the over six-month high of $90.6 touched on August 26th amid risks to supply and strong demand.
The outlook on yellowcake supply from Kazatomprom, the world's largest uranium producer, faced fresh uncertainty as its TQZ sulphuric acid plant faced delays, limiting capacity for leaching uranium.

The producer also noted that demand was accelerating as large economies continued to invest in nuclear power to achieve decarbonization goals and limit exposure to volatile commodity markets due to geopolitical tension in Russia and the Middle East. Italy was the latest to express interest to approve a legal framework to restore nuclear power, in line with measures from the US and Japan as power consumers expand sources for generation to account for the higher demand from data center projects.
Meta, Amazon, and Microsoft signed agreements to gain fresh nuclear capacity for their future AI data center operations.

title: Uranium Holds Near 6-Month High
